note: AI-platform software subscriptions carried on top of the infrastructure options, per SPEC §7.4. This is NOT a fourth comparison option: a platform licence is a cost layer on the options that actually run a platform, and SPEC §2.1 is explicit that there are three options and no fourth.
provenance_contract: PROVENANCE IS PER FIELD IN THIS FILE, not per row, and the two halves have different authorities. The METER (how the vendor counts what you owe) is `first_party` — it is quoted verbatim from the vendor's own licensing documentation, with the URL. The AMOUNT is not: no vendor in this file publishes a list price for these products, so every price is either `indicative` (a cited secondary figure) or null (unpublished — the user supplies their quote). A documented meter must never lend its authority to an undocumented amount, so a row with a first_party meter and a null price is the NORMAL shape here, not a gap to be filled with a plausible number.

meters.per_gpu_ram_gb_year: One entitlement per GB of GPU memory, summed across every GPU in the cluster, per year.
meters.per_gpu_year: One entitlement per physical GPU, per year.
meters.per_gpu_hour: One entitlement per physical GPU, per hour of use (cloud marketplace / pay-as-you-go).
meters.per_accelerator_year: One entitlement per physical accelerator (GPU or TPU), per year. CPU core counts do not affect it.
meters.per_vcpu_year: One entitlement per vCPU on worker nodes running inference, per year. Used when a cluster has no GPU accelerators.
meters.per_node_year: One entitlement per physical node, per year.
meters.per_user_month: One entitlement per named user, per month.
meters.flat_month: A single negotiated figure per month, independent of any fleet or headcount.

derivable_note: The meters listed above are DERIVED from the fleet this calculator already sizes — GPU count comes from demand.js:gpusForLoad and per-GPU memory from gpu-pricing.json:gpus[].vram_gb — so the licence cost moves when the fleet moves instead of sitting as a stale figure the user typed once. per_vcpu_year, per_node_year, per_user_month and flat_month are NOT derivable from anything the calculator models, and their quantity is entered.

rows.label: No platform subscription
rows.note: The default. Self-managed vLLM/SGLang with no vendor platform licence.

rows.label: Nutanix Enterprise AI (NAI) Pro
rows.meter_quote: NAI is metered by either aggregate GPU RAM for inference clusters with GPUs installed*, or by vCPUs used by worker nodes running inferencing for clusters with no GPU accelerators.
rows.meter_quote_2: *GPU RAM GB license is provided in 1 GB entitlement increments that are quantified across all GPUs in a cluster.
rows.note: Applies to the rented option as well as the owned one: NAI Standalone is documented as running on any CNCF-certified Kubernetes anywhere, including public clouds. Nutanix publishes no list price for NAI, so the per-GB figure is yours to enter from your quote — the meter is what this row contributes, and it is the reason the cost recomputes as your fleet's aggregate GPU RAM changes.

rows.label: NVIDIA AI Enterprise — annual subscription (self-managed)
rows.price_note: A secondary citation, not a vendor price list. NVIDIA publishes the METER but not the amount. Reported figures ladder from about $4,500 to $18,000 per GPU per year depending on term and support tier, so treat this as the bottom of a range.
rows.meter_quote: NVIDIA AI Enterprise software is licensed on a per-GPU basis. A software license is required for every GPU installed on the server or workstation that will host any software that is included with NVIDIA AI Enterprise.
bundled_exemptions: Each NVIDIA H100 PCIe or NVL Tensor Core GPU includes a five-year NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription.
Each NVIDIA H200 NVL Tensor Core GPU includes a five-year NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription.
Each NVIDIA A800 40GB Active GPU includes a three-year NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription.
NVIDIA AI Enterprise is included in the NVIDIA DGX software bundle for DGX systems using the Hopper architecture; Blackwell DGX systems must purchase it separately.

bundled_server_ids.dgx-h100-gpufm: NVIDIA AI Enterprise is included in the DGX software bundle for Hopper-architecture DGX systems.
bundled_server_ids.pcie-h100-4x-gpufm: Each NVIDIA H100 PCIe Tensor Core GPU includes a five-year NVIDIA AI Enterprise subscription.

rows.bundled_match_note: Matched by server_id, never by gpu_id. The exemption is a property of the SKU, not the accelerator family: an H100 PCIe card carries the entitlement and an H100 SXM in an HGX node does not, and both are gpu_id h100. The HGX and DGX-Blackwell rows are deliberately absent — the vendor states Blackwell DGX systems must purchase it separately.
rows.note: DOUBLE-COUNTING HAZARD, documented by the vendor: several SKUs already include this subscription. Pairing this row with the dgx-h100-gpufm server config charges a licence the Hopper DGX bundle already carries. The exemptions are listed so the UI can warn instead of silently overcharging, and bundled_server_ids is the machine-actionable form app.js:bundledExemptionFor reads. The warning does NOT zero the charge: the bundle is a fixed five- or three-year entitlement while this row is an annual subscription, so the honest act is to tell the buyer the overlap exists and let them price it.

rows.label: NVIDIA AI Enterprise — cloud marketplace (pay-as-you-go)
rows.meter_quote: NVIDIA AI Enterprise in cloud marketplaces is priced per GPU per hour on an on-demand/pay-as-you-go basis.
rows.note: Rented option only — this is the marketplace meter, and it is charged against the same rented GPU-hours the rented option already computes, not against a wall-clock month.

rows.label: Red Hat AI Inference Server
rows.meter_quote: Red Hat AI Inference and Red Hat Enterprise Linux® AI are accelerator-centric. These products are licensed per physical accelerator, such as GPU and tensor processing unit (TPU), CPU core counts do not affect the subscription cost.
rows.note: Red Hat publishes the counting rule but not the price. Enter your quoted per-accelerator figure.

rows.label: Red Hat OpenShift AI (layered add-on)
rows.meter_quote: Red Hat OpenShift® AI is a layered add-on.
rows.note: INCOMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION: OpenShift AI layers on an underlying OpenShift platform subscription counted in core-pairs or bare-metal nodes, which this calculator does not model. Selecting this row prices the AI Accelerator SKUs only, and the UI says so — it is not the whole OpenShift bill.

rows.label: Per-seat AI subscription (generic)
rows.note: For seat-metered tooling paid per named user regardless of how inference is served, which is why it applies to all three options. The quantity is the user count already entered in the demand model.

rows.label: Custom — flat monthly
rows.note: An escape hatch for a negotiated figure that no meter in this file describes. It is deliberately NOT derived from anything, and is labelled as entered rather than derived at every point of use.
